acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Mummies family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Pharaoh's Champion, T4, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Death-Mask Tomb Formation Marshal (Champion) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two water construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: A fully wrapped elite in ceremonial armor with a complete gold death-mask, four visible retaining straps, a broad collar, and family-native tomb sand circling only its stiff footwork.

Signature mechanic: Four-Faced Tomb: the Champion's full death-mask turns toward a cardinal side while ceremonial armor plates unfold along that edge. Husks trail snare strips across one flank, Tomb Guards cross the front, and a Sacred Servant writes a return path behind. Sand disturbed at their feet records every occupied line but has no independent elemental force. The opposite mask strap stretches visibly under the formation load.
battlefieldDuty: Assemble lower Mummies into a four-sided tomb formation by turning its gold death-mask toward one side and directing native sand only as a readable footprint record.
constructionDimensions: Preservation becomes hydraulic through resin-dark wet linen, sealed alabaster reservoirs, shell or silver valves, fluid-filled glyph channels, and pressure bladders fitted beneath collars, armor, and sarcophagus hardware.
Actions show coherent filling and drainage through tightening saturated wraps, wet reflection, narrow jets along glyph paths, lifted valves, and slackening linen when pressure is lost.
counterplay: Move through the side before the armor edge closes, avoid the familiar lower-form lines, and cut the rear mask strap; each broken strap prevents the Champion from rebuilding that side. Affinity signal: An alabaster reservoir fills toward the active limb or seal and its valve rises; opening it drains that route and exposes the underlying knot or dried joint.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only water treatment without saturated materials, reservoirs, and pressure behavior
Glow-only water treatment without coherent channels, valves, and drainage
Shapeless blue wrapping or a liquid corpse that erases linen construction
Mist or spray that conceals glyph order, knots, mask straps, or sarcophagus tells
identityInvariants: A stiff-limbed human or humanoid silhouette remains wrapped from head to foot, with arms held forward, crossed, guarding, inscribing, or commanding through readable linen tension.
Sun-bleached linen, sand beige, desert ochre, deep gold, lapis blue, and turquoise remain funerary materials and symbols rather than affinity colors.
Linen bandage, dried flesh, gold leaf, lapis, carnelian, bronze, and sandstone grave goods stay materially distinct and retain visible knots, stitches, glyph routes, and breakable seals.
Family-native sand and dust follow disturbed wrappings, tomb movement, and burial objects without becoming Earth or Wind affinity by themselves.
Escalation adds precious thread, glyph density, collars, masks, armor, headdresses, and sarcophagus regalia while the bandages never come off and always explain binding and counterplay.
telegraph: The gold mask rotates with a dry click, one armor edge opens, native sand swirls only around moving feet, and the opposite linen strap pulls away from the wrapped skull.
